video.title: This AI Finds Cheap Products You Can Sell for 5x More

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates going from a physical product idea to a sourced product in one sitting, using the AI sourcing agent Accio (transcribed 'Axio'). He validates demand for a discreet 'porch pirate' parcel box via Google Trends, searches Accio in natural language, generates a tech pack, and compares supplier prices to Amazon listings. He claims a $27 sourced box sells for $143 on Amazon, about 75-80% gross margin and 20-30% net after shipping and fees. The video is sponsored by Accio, so the takeaway is that sourcing and validation tools make starting a physical product business faster, but the numbers are an unverified back-of-envelope demo.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; sponsored by Accio for this video

ideas.name: Discreet porch parcel box (sourced and resold)
ideas.one_liner: Import an existing wooden-look lockable delivery box from an overseas supplier and resell it on Amazon, Facebook Marketplace and Shopify.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales at retail markup (buy wholesale, resell)
ideas.customer: Homeowners worried about package theft (porch piracy)
ideas.problem: Parcels left on the porch get stolen; existing parcel lockers are ugly and commercial.
ideas.offer: A secure, weatherproof, lockable delivery box styled like outdoor furniture (wood grain, wicker or iron) that looks like it belongs on a porch.

pricing.model: Retail resale at a markup over landed supplier cost

price_points.label: Supplier cost of top sourced wooden delivery box
Amazon retail price of the identical-looking box

pricing.notes: Host claims about 75-80% gross margin and 20-30% net profit after shipping and Amazon fees.

acquisition_channels.details: List on Amazon, where the sourced-box lookalikes already sell hundreds per month, and on Facebook Marketplace (listed within 5 minutes, inquiries in 10-15).

quote.text: Facebook Marketplace. The good old trusty standby where you can have something listed within five minutes and you can have inquiries within 10 or 15.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Own Shopify site pushed with Google, Facebook and Instagram ads.
Viral content using anger, hilarity and curiosity angles (like Mark Rober's glitter bomb videos); use supplier samples to shoot photos and videos before ordering stock.

quote.text: those are the same marketing angles that we're going to use to sell this.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Supplier on Alibaba or similar manufactures and ships the product; the seller imports, stores and fulfils orders (or uses Amazon fulfilment). Optional custom design via an AI-generated tech pack sent to a manufacturer.
unit_economics_claims: $27 sourced vs $143 Amazon retail, roughly 75-80% gross margin
Net profit 20-30% after shipping and Amazon fees
Top lookalike listings sold 100-500+ units in the last month
ideas.startup_cost: About $2,700 for a 100-unit minimum order, or a free or roughly $100 sample first
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated (Facebook Marketplace listing possible within minutes once stock or samples exist)

acquisition.how: Marketplace listings, SEO and paid ads can be agent-run and the content can be AI-assisted, but viral content needs creative human input.

onboarding.how: Ecommerce checkout needs no onboarding; supplier inquiries are auto-filled and auto-replied by Accio.

delivery.how: Physical goods need import, customs, warehousing and shipping; Amazon FBA or a 3PL can reduce handling but not remove it.

billing.how: Marketplace and Shopify payments are automatic.

support.how: Agents can handle order and returns queries; damaged goods and returns are physical and need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Parcel theft and parcel boxes exist in the UK too and the sourcing method is the same. Needs UK/EU import duty and VAT, UKCA/CE and product safety checks, Amazon UK and eBay or Facebook Marketplace UK. 'Porch' and 'parcel box' terms and US search trends need re-checking in UK Google Trends.

risks: Undifferentiated lookalike product competes on price with many identical sellers
Net margin of 20-30% is thin once ads, returns and FX are included
The 100-unit MOQ ties up about $2,700 before demand is proven
Supplier quality and weatherproofing claims unverified
Amazon prices and sales numbers can be gamed or short-lived
Import duty and compliance not discussed

tactics.name: Validate product demand with Google Trends then refine keywords
steps: Search the problem phrase (porch pirate) in Google Trends over 5 and 22 years
Search the product phrase (porch pirate box) to see if recent interest is rising
Use the category names the sourcing AI returns (parcel box, parcel locker) and check them in Trends too

quote.text: I'm going to go over here to Google Trends, search parcel boxes, and that too is up and to the right.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Price-check supplier results against Amazon
steps: Search the product category on Amazon and note sponsored versus organic listings
Check whether residential versions are advertised; gaps signal opportunity
Compare supplier price to top Amazon price for gross margin
Use a third-party Amazon photo search app with the supplier image URLs to find exact replicas
Check units sold last month on top listings

quote.text: copy the URLs of all these pictures that Axio spits out and search for them through this third party app
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use AI to analyse why one identical listing outsells another
steps: Screenshot two similar listings side by side
Upload to an AI and ask why one sold more
Remove sales numbers and ask which sold more to avoid bias

quote.text: screenshot each of these side by side, upload them to AI and say, "Why did the one on the right sell more than the one on the left?"
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Sample before committing to a minimum order
steps: Find a vendor who sends a free or about $100 sample
Shoot photos and videos with the sample
Test demand with content before ordering the 100-unit MOQ

tactics.name: Generate a tech pack with AI for a custom variant
steps: Choose a base design from the sourcing results
Prompt the AI to build a full tech pack with new finish and materials
Send the tech pack to manufacturers to quote a custom product

quote.text: before going all in and spending $2,700 on a hundred of these things before you really know if there's demand yet.

warnings.warning: Anecdotal evidence of demand may not be real evidence, so check data such as Google Trends.

quote.text: my anecdotal evidence might not be real evidence.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Check demand with search-trend data before investing in a product idea rather than relying on gut feel.
Ride a rising trend with a narrower product phrase; interest in the specific product term can be exploding even when the broad problem is flat.

quote.text: over the last 9 months, it is exploding in popularity. So, we want to ride a mega trend.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Sourcing an existing product instead of designing and manufacturing one removes the hardest steps for a first physical product.
Sponsored listings of commercial versions with no ads for residential versions hint at an underserved niche, and advertisers imply the category is profitable.

quote.text: they wouldn't be paying for ads if the products weren't profitable even after accounting for the ads.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Gross margin looks big but net after shipping, fees and ads is much smaller (20-30% claimed), so model net margin before ordering.
Emotional viral content angles (anger, humour, curiosity) can be a cheap acquisition route for physical products.
AI agents can automate supplier discovery, inquiries and spec documents, shrinking the gap between idea and selling a product.

quote.text: the gap between I have an idea and I'm selling a physical product has never been this small.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Time-zone gaps with Asian suppliers mean auto-replies and overnight responses speed up supplier communication.

evidence_quality.rationale: Sponsored product demo, not a real operating business. The margin figures come from comparing one supplier listing and one Amazon listing, with no actual orders, shipping, fees, ad costs or sales; the net margin is an unsupported estimate.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsored by Accio (host says they support the channel); includes a free-trial link and prompts in the bio.
